messages:
ryan (oncall): node-monitor-bot alerted ~3m ago: APS4a-GPU-120 had a sudden PCIe link drop and soft-reboot loop. Opening thread to coordinate a safe drain and capacity shift. @maria @chris please triage :warning:
node-monitor-bot: ALERT: aps4a-gpu-120 kernel panic x3 within 8m. Marking node UNHEALTHY and incrementing failcount.
maria: seeing repeated kernel oops in system logs, looks like firmware/hardware. No recent deploys to that host.
chris: noticed ~12% capacity drop in APS4a GPU pool; request queues for small-seq models spiked 15%. Autoscaler didnt trigger because pod eviction stalled.
jamie: starting soft drain now to avoid OOMs: running ->
```
redwoodctl drain-node aps4a-gpu-120 --grace=30 --evict-pods
```
jamie: drain job started, moving 8 model containers. routing fallback targets: aps4b, eu-west-1.
ops-bot: ops-bot started job 3179: draining aps4a-gpu-120 -> redispatch 8 pods to fallback pools. Estimated 120s to finish.
ryan (oncall): plan: 1) soft-drain node, 2) reroute new allocations for latency-sensitive routes to eu-west until pool stable, 3) mark node for hardware replacement and remove from autoscale group. Approving immediate reroute.
maria: reroute executed for routes tagged latency-sensitive. Note: some customers will see cross-region egress; pinging finance for cost impact. @finance-team
finance-team: acknowledged. quick estimate: extra egress ~ $0.02/token equivalent for affected flows if sustained. Keep us posted.
chris: quick check: dedicated reserved pools are at 78% in us-west; we can burst a couple of small jobs there but it will increase tail latency for other tenants. Recommend using eu-west fallback first.
jamie: opening internal ticket INF-4321: "APS4a GPU node hardware failure -> replacement". Scheduling hardware replacement, spare ETA ~48h from inventory. Marking node as DECOMMISSION_PENDING.
ryan (oncall): after drain, please trigger rolling restarts of impacted model servers to clear KV caches and ensure no stale state. Watch for 503s.
maria: I'll monitor model latency and error rates for 30 minutes. Set temporary alert: model_latency_p99_increase > 10% -> page oncall.
jamie: drain finished, all pods redistributed. node now cordoned. logs show PCIe reset events before kernel panic.
ops-bot: ops-bot: redistributed 8 pods: 5->aps4b, 3->eu-west-1. No failed migrations.
chris: queues returning to normal, latency back within SLO for most routes. Small spike remains for a shard that landed in us-west-dedicated; moving that shard to eu-west now.
ryan (oncall): good work. next steps: replace hardware, follow up with firmware vendor about PCIe link flakiness, update runbook with this failure pattern, and confirm autoscaler behavior on drain stalls. Assigning post-incident owner: jamie.
maria: adding runbook note and a short blameless postmortem draft.
jamie: making INF-4321 link and scheduling hardware swap. will update when spare arrives.
ryan (oncall): closing loop here — keep thread updated if performance regresses. :thumbsup:
